Communication
Students read, understand, and interpret Latin or Greek.
Beginning Stage (Level 1)
Read and recognize simple written words, and phases in Latin and /or Greek with appropriate guidance.
Recognize and identify essential grammatical structures to understand and translate simple phrases and/or sentences in Latin and/or Greek.
Read and understand Latin and/or Greek words and/or simple sentences in passages using dictionaries and/or thesaurus.
Recognize and identify specific factual information in selected Latin and/or Greek simple passages.
Demonstrate understanding of the general tone in selected Latin and/or Greek simple passages.
Recognize and identify basic common Latin and/or Greek abbreviations as being used in contemporary American English or other modern world languages.
Developing Stage (Levels 2 & 3)
*Perform required skills from previous stage and* read and understand short adapted or un-adapted prose passages or simple poetry in Latin and/or Greek with some appropriate guidance.

*Perform required skills from previous stage and* apply understanding of grammatical structures including declension, verb conjugation, and syntax to comprehend and translate prose passages and/or simple poetry in Latin and/or Greek.
*Perform required skills from previous stage and* read and show understanding of Latin and/or Greek words and sentences from selected texts using dictionaries, thesaurus, and derivatives.
*Perform required skills from previous stage and* demonstrate understanding of specific factual information and main ideas in selected Latin and/or Greek texts.
*Perform required skills from previous stage and* understand and analyze the general tone and meaning implied of selected Latin and/or Greek texts.
*Perform required skills from previous stage and* understand common Latin and/or Greek abbreviations, sentences, and/or mottoes used in contemporary English usage or other modern world languages.
Expanding Stages (Levels 4 & 5)
*Perform required skills from previous stage and* understand and interpret prose and poetry of Latin and/or Greek authors with little guidance.

*Perform required skills from previous stage and* interpret and analyze complex grammatical structures and literary devices to comprehend, interpret, and translate prose and poetry from Latin and/or Greek authors.
*Perform required skills from previous stage and* analyze and infer the implied meaning of Latin and/or Greek words, phrases, and sentences in authentic texts using derivatives and context clues.
*Perform required skills from previous stage and* analyze specific factual information, main ideas, and supporting details in authentic Latin and/or Greek texts.
*Perform required skills from previous stage and* evaluate and infer the tone and implied meaning of authentic Latin and/or Greek texts.

*Perform required skills from previous stage and* analyze and apply Latin and/or Greek abbreviations, sentences, mottoes and/or literary, and technical terms as appropriate in any contemporary language usage.

Respond to basic commands in classroom settings using appropriate gestures.
Ask and answer signed simple questions about basic personal information and the students’ immediate environment.
Exchange basic personal information with emphasis in the present tense frames.
Initiate brief exchanges using basic language signs, familiar phrases, and sentences.

*Perform required skills from previous stage and* ask and respond to clarify information regarding routine, familiar activities, and factual questions on common topics.
*Perform required skills from previous stage and* exchange information and ideas on everyday topics with emphasis on present, past, and future time frames.

*Perform required skills from previous stage and* initiate, sustain, and close exchanges applying familiar signs, recombined sentences, structures, and non-manual markers (i.e., facial grammar, mouth phonemes and morphemes) to new situations.

*Perform required skills from previous stage and* engage in original and spontaneous communications on various topics with emphasis on a variety of time frames, and contemporary and historical events and issues.

*Perform required skills from previous stage and* engage in and sustain exchanges applying new complex non-manual markers, registers, classifiers, cultural behaviors, and structures to common and new situations.
